rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a baseline built from first principles. Geometry: five line sensors spaced 10 mm apart across x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the tape. Sensor size is 12 mm, which covers the 25 mm tape with some margin. Sensor weights are proportional to sensor x (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal is the reading-weighted lateral position of the tape, with positive meaning left. Body and wheel values are a mid-range, stable platform: wheel_track 0.12 m for moderate yaw authority, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg. Controller: kp = 4 gives a moderate steering response (about 1400 PWM per unit of signal). kd = 0.4 damps the oscillation from the sensor lag. ki = 0.05 is small, since the course has no persistent offset to remove. base_speed = 1.6 (throttle 0.8 of full PWM) aims at the roughly 1.5 m/s average the 3 s limit requires, while leaving room to slow on the tighter bends. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the tape. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. The next race should show whether speed is limiting finish time or whether the robot leaves the track on the sharper bends.
